clauses.reason: The operative paragraph of Executive Order 8369 further exempts Louis A. Simon from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, for a term it states as 'for a period of one year ending May 31, 1941'. The exemption is a fixed-term command, so it ends by its own terms on the stated date, 1941-05-31. The date is recorded inclusive, as the exemption runs through the end of May 31, 1941; the exclusive reading, under which the term ends when that day begins, is the alternative. The grant is personal to one named person and nothing in the held text makes it depend on a report, an event or a later order. A later order, Executive Order 8747 dated April 28, 1941, recites this order and grants a further exemption 'for a period of six months ending November 30, 1941'. It is recorded as a later event with its own date. It is a separate command and does not end this order's term, which is the stated term of this order alone. The recital cites the earlier exemption orders Executive Order 7581 of March 19, 1937, Executive Order 7824 of February 25, 1938, Executive Order 8046 of February 11, 1939 as predecessors; they precede this order and are not events affecting it.

The held text of Executive Order 8747 grants a further exemption and neither revokes this order nor shortens its stated term, so it is recorded as a later event and not as an end.
